author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Fix audio crackle, latency, and synchronization problems
summary: Separate underruns caused by low emulation speed from output-latency problems, test a stable buffer, and avoid hiding timing faults with asynchronous audio modes.
heroAlt: PCSX2 SPU2 reverb visualization from an audio-system development report

blocks.text: First decide whether audio is the victim or the cause

When emulation falls below full speed, the audio stream may starve, stretch or repeat even though the SPU2 path is correct. A separate class of problem occurs when Android's output buffer is too small for the device, Bluetooth adds delay, or another app seizes audio focus. Treat crackle, latency and drift as distinct symptoms and test them against emulation speed.
Keep synchronized audio mode and the default buffer until full emulation speed has been proved. Async modes can make sound appear smooth while game timing remains wrong.

Use wired speakers or the device speaker for the baseline because Bluetooth adds codec buffering. Restore Safe performance settings, native resolution and normal game speed. Choose a scene with continuous music plus a visible input response so crackle and lip/input delay can be judged separately.

items: Full-speed baseline attempt on Safe settings.
Bluetooth disabled for the first comparison.
Fixed system volume below clipping.
A scene with continuous audio and visible timing cues.
No screen recorder or voice chat holding audio focus.

blocks.text: Separate speed, buffer, and output-path faults

items: 1. Watch emulation speed when the crackle occurs. If speed drops at the same moment, fix the performance limit first.
2. At full speed, raise audio latency/buffer one supported step and repeat the scene; do not also change synchronization mode.
3. Compare device speaker or wired output with Bluetooth. A constant Bluetooth delay is an output path characteristic, not an emulation timing failure.
4. Return the buffer to the lowest value that stays clean for ten minutes, including a scene transition.
5. Test pause/resume and Android focus changes, then save an audio exception per game only if the fault is title-specific.

blocks.text: A valid fix produces clean continuous audio while emulation stays at the intended speed and sound remains aligned with visible events. It must survive a warm session, pause/resume and one app-background cycle. Volume amplification should not clip; test at normal gain before blaming the buffer.

items: Crackle does not coincide with emulation-speed loss.
Wired/device output is clean at a documented buffer.
Pause and resume do not introduce permanent drift.
Bluetooth behaviour is recorded separately.
No async mode masks slow gameplay.

blocks.text: Restore synchronized mode and the previous buffer if timing drifts or controls feel delayed. Close other audio apps and restart the device after an audio-service fault. Reset only the game's audio profile; do not delete memory cards, shader caches or graphics settings for an output problem.

items: Restore default sync and latency.
Disable Bluetooth and retest locally.
Stop recording/communication apps.
Reset the per-game audio override.
Crackle tracks FPS drops: solve CPU/GPU/thermal speed first.
Only Bluetooth is delayed: codec and radio buffering dominate.
High volume distorts everywhere: output clipping, not emulation sync.
Audio becomes smooth but game timing drifts: async mode hid the real fault.

blocks.text: Keep the final note short: output device, buffer, sync mode, game serial and whether full speed was maintained. That evidence prevents the same crackle from being 'fixed' repeatedly with larger buffers when the underlying cause is a performance drop.
